subject: Suspicious auth attempts — request for IRP evidence & SOC 2 mapping
body:
From: security@northbridge.com
To: michael.grant@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:22 -0700
Subject: Notification: Suspicious API auth attempts - Redwood account NB-423

Hi Michael / Marissa —

We detected a burst of failed API key attempts against our Redwood tenant NB-423 between 08:45 and 09:05 PDT this morning. Attempts originated from a small set of IPs that do not match our expected allowlist. No data exfiltration detected on our side, but we are preserving telemetry while we investigate.

What we need from you immediately:
- Confirmation that you are preserving server-side telemetry for NB-423 and a short manifest of the artifacts you will produce (auth logs, token issuance history, access logs).
- A copy or pointer to your IRP (incident response plan) contacts and escalation steps we should expect while we coordinate.
- SOC 2 mapping: which control families cover auth anomalies and log retention windows (we need to confirm this against our compliance requirements).

Ticket: NB-423-8873 (internal)
We may need an evidence package for our auditors within the next 5 business days.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Security Operations
NorthBridge Capital
security@northbridge.com

---

From: michael.grant@redwood.ai
To: security@northbridge.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:34:56 -0700
Subject: Re: Notification: Suspicious API auth attempts - Redwood account NB-423

Lena —

Thanks for the heads up and for preserving the ticket. Quick status from our side:
- We have started a preservation job for NB-423 telemetry and locked a read-only export snapshot from 08:30–09:30 PDT. I attached the preservation_manifest.txt with the artifact list (auth logs, API gateway request logs, token lifecycle events, and instance-level telemetry).
- Our IRP contacts for customer-facing incidents are listed below; I will also open a dedicated incident channel and invite your SOC and our on-call responders.

Redwood incident coordinator (primary): Michael Grant — michael.grant@redwood.ai, +1 415-555-0119
Redwood incident responder (security lead): Marissa Cole — marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Engineering on-call (infra): Karthik Iyer — karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

For SOC 2 mapping: we maintain controls under CC6 (Logical and Physical Access Controls) and CC7 (System Operations) that cover authentication monitoring and log retention. I don't have a formal mapping doc attached to this message; if you want we can pull a short control-mapping snapshot for NB-423 (should be <24 hours).

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) I will provide a read-only evidence bundle with redacted PII by EOD (today).
2) We will run a quick token-issue audit and reply with any anomalous token creation within the window.
3) If you need the full, unredacted artifact set for your auditors, please confirm a retention exception and an approved SOW/NDAs so we can provision access securely.

Attaching: preservation_manifest.txt (artifact index)

Michael
Incident Response Coordinator
Redwood Inference

---

On Mon, May 18, 2026 at 11:02 AM PDT security@northbridge.com wrote:
> Hi Michael —
>
> Thanks for the quick turnaround and the manifest — appreciated. We opened an internal request to our compliance team to confirm whether they need full unredacted artifacts. At minimum they want:
> - The IRP contact list (for our SOC to join the incident bridge)
> - A short SOC 2 control crosswalk indicating which Redwood controls cover auth monitoring/retention
> - A timeframe for when we can expect the redacted bundle (EOD sounds fine)
>
> We also copied AuditLane (support@auditlane.io) who may request the evidence package directly for the audit queue. Ticket NB-423-8873 is now live on our side.
>
> For retention exception — our auditors will need a signed attestation that Redwood will hold the unredacted artifacts for 30 days; please advise who on your legal/compliance team we should coordinate with.
>
> Lena Ortiz
> NorthBridge Capital

---

From: michael.grant@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 08:09:01 -0700
Subject: Internal: NB-423 auth anomaly — IRP evidence, retention exception request

Folks —

Summary: NorthBridge detected a burst of failed API key attempts this morning (ticket NB-423-8873). They requested preserved telemetry, our IRP contact list, and a SOC 2 crosswalk. They may request full artifacts for AuditLane.

What I did: preservation snapshot taken, manifest attached earlier; offered to produce redacted evidence by EOD; asked for confirmation on retention exception if they need unredacted artifacts for auditors.

Asks for you:
- Marissa: can you confirm which SOC 2 control matrix doc we can safely share as a CC6/CC7 crosswalk? If we can produce the one-pager, I’ll send it to Lena and AuditLane.
- Karthik: please run the token-issue audit for NB-423 and flag any token issuances originating outside of expected geos or service accounts. If you find anything, paste results in SEC-431 and mark priority.
- Legal/compliance: we will need a retention-exception approval template and the signatory (who can commit to 30-day secure hold) — if Legal needs to loop, I can open a request.

Proposed timeline: redacted bundle by 2026-05-18 EOD (we may already miss EOD; push target to 2026-05-19 14:00 PDT), SOC 2 crosswalk by EOD 2026-05-19, retention exception template same day.

I will coordinate the incident bridge if NorthBridge asks to escalate. Also recommend we prepare a short postmortem/share packet (IRP_summary_v1.pdf) in case auditors ask for an after-action.

Michael Grant
Incident Response Coordinator
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced in thread:
- preservation_manifest.txt (index of preserved artifacts)
- nb_ticket_8873.json (NorthBridge ticket reference)
- IRP_summary_v1.pdf (post-incident outline for external share)
